title: Open Sesame
subtitle: An incantation is not always what opens the door to a cave of treasure.

items.text: Inside the Sharma Old House

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: How is everything now?

items.speaker: Ms. Sherjah
items.text: Well, it's going smooth. The young people and tourists left as soon as I persuaded them. Only the old and the children are left here. It's not that easy for them to move, and ...

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: Hey, you promised to give me half of it! Now what, the boss cannot keep her own promise?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Humph! I do most messenger work! More food for more work!

items.speaker: Ms. Sherjah
items.text: These kids were abandoned and driven away by humans. I'm glad to see Kanjira get along with them.
Kaalaa Baunaa looks down at the astrolabe in her hand.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: If she could enjoy a life like this ...

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: No. Nothing.
Kaalaa Baunaa chuckles. There's a faraway look on her face.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: You just reminded me of my mother.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Sherjah, perhaps people like you are the key to saving all of us.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I just observed it again. The figures are showing a grim picture. Luckily, I've worked out the specific range of damage.
She draws quite a large circle on the map.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: As long as we can get out of this radius, there will be no casualties.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: As for other losses ... they are beyond my ability to cover.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Emm.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: The airship of the Foundation is on the way. At least our water supply is secured for now.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: But the problem is, in such a distance ...
She draws a straight line on the map lightly.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: The distance ... Even if we follow the straight line, it is impossible for us, with the elders and the children, to get out of it within hours.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: Err, why! We are getting so close to success.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: If only we could go underground ...

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Underground? Wait!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: I remember my old man told me about an emergency tunnel leading to the forest on the mountain. Its entrance is right here, beneath the floor of this very room.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: A tunnel?

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: He told me this, hoping that one day I will take over his responsibility to look after the village. If I remember it correctly, that forest, which is also the exit of this tunnel, is right outside the impact area.
He taps on a spot outside the marked range with his rough finger.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That's great. In the tunnel, even if we don't make it to the forest in time, we can still avoid the damage.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: But, but ...
He scratches his beard, hissing in embarrassment.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: The problem is there's a gate to the tunnel. Now, just for the record, I'm only quoting my old man.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: "It is a gate which only opens to the leader who has earned his people's trust."

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Oh, "Open Sesame!" We is going real treasure hunting this time.
Out of the silence, only the naive child is excited.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Oh, well. My father's version was hardly as exciting as "Open Sesame"! I didn't believe him even as a child!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: I tried to open it by force many times. Well, it never worked!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: If my old man was telling the truth, things would be problematic for us …

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Because I don't think I can get that gate open! Firstly, I've never wanted to be a leader, and speaking of "the people's trust" ... How do you think those cursing old men in the yard will feel about me?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Emm.
Kaalaa Baunaa listens to "those cursing old men" for a while. She cannot contradict what he says.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Even so ...
She taps on the map, thinking.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: We will open that gate.
She looks up at Shamane. He is standing in silence and has a blank look on his face.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Even if we have to smash it with our bare fists.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: I'm not sure if you were being sarcastic.
She doesn't give a clear answer. Instead, her eyes flit back to the map.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: It's the best way in the current situation.
On the porch in front of the house, there is a loose floorboard.
Under it, they see some wooden stairs, which appear to be the entrance of a tunnel.

items.speaker: Ms. Sherjah
items.text: Watch your steps.
One after another, they slowly go down the stairs.
In Front of the Stone Gate
The gray and yellow stone gate has a pattern of an elephant raising its front feet in the middle. It is as immovable as a real elephant.

items.speaker: Matilda
items.text: So the spell Shamane told us is truly useless.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hahaha, what did I say? This is never the gate for me to open.
Shamane gives them an embarrassed smile. Behind him, the criticism comes as expected.

items.speaker: Takal
items.text: Tsk, I knew we shouldn't have counted on you, Sharma boy. You can't even protect your own family. How are you supposed to protect others?

items.speaker: Villager 2
items.text: May the gods listen to my prayer and send us another guide ...
Oh, here they come again! The complaints Shamane has heard so many times. Those familiar syllables make him almost—nostalgic.
Kanjira is tapping a foot faster and faster—it's getting hard for her to suppress the anger.

items.speaker: Takal
items.text: After dealing with humans all these years, we are already ...

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: SHUT UP YOUR MOUTHS!!
The crowd instantly falls into silence.
The spell of "nostalgia" is broken. Shamane lowers his head, surprised by her irritation.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: All you talk about is protect, family, and stuff. Give me a break!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: And YOU!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Emm? Me?
Shamane points at his own nose, brought up short.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Yes, you!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: W-what about me?
Kanjira throws back her head and glares at him.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You love talking, don't you? Now you go dumb? Humph! Big guy can't defend yourself!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I just don't understand. You feel bad. You say it. Why is you afraid?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You don't owe them!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: See?
Kanjira extends a finger at the hushed crowd.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: You talk, and you shut them up!
Shamane follows her pointing finger and looks at the familiar faces.
He suddenly realizes that, after all these years, he still remembers each of them clearly.
There is no longer anger or disdain in their eyes. They just remain silent and avoid his gaze.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Why don't you do this earlier? We need to focus on the most important thing!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: It's "Open Sesame" story!
Kanjira mumbles admiringly.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: In the story, only the most smart and wise people can open it! Why do you hesitate now?

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Haha ...
Shamane laughs, as if she has said something most amusing.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Little one, you think I'm the smartest and wisest person?

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Er, no.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Oh.
His laugh stops.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: But why ask me? It is your gate!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: My answer don't matter. Their answer don't matter, too. That's why I said you should shut them up!
Kanjira rolls her eyes.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: There will be a gate for me, and I will open it my way!

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm the one to decide how to open my gate. My spell will be longer and cooler than some "Open Sesame."

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: I'm not jealous you!
She turns her back to him, refusing to cast a look at him.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Haha ... *sighs* Interesting! Looks like Dad was right. I'm not qualified to be a leader.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Thanks, kid.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Phew!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Anyway, times have changed. Forget the spell.
That's his father's gate, his father's path, his father's choice of life, and his father's responsibility.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: But it is I who am standing here, not him.
He raises his voice.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Screw it. I have no idea what my father once promised you. In fact, I have no interest in what your old heads think.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hmm, but what's my own way of opening the gate?
Pick a new spell? Sing a song? Bleat like a goat?
His fist clenches. At this serious, crucial moment, he is strangely relieved by one sudden idea.
He doesn't need any implements. He can just do it with his bare hands, figuratively and literally.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hahaha!

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: And the one standing right here right now is me, not another Sharma.
Keep the shoulder loose, stay steady, and engage with the upper arm.
This is his way.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: That is to say ...

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Hah!
This is the easiest punch he has ever thrown.
The burden from the past, the pain, and the stress are thrown out of his body at this moment.
Oh! Turns out the gate ...
... is much more fragile than I thought.
Forest on the Backslope
It's a quiet night in the forest. A bonfire is lit in a small, open space.

items.speaker: Ajar
items.text: "That is to say, I'll smash that door open, even if it takes the other arm of mine!"

items.speaker: Villager 3
items.text: Yes! That's what I'm talking about. So cool!
As the stick pokes the bonfire, a clear snap can be heard.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I guess you didn't see that coming?

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: To tell the truth, I had prepared myself to bounce off from that closed gate, like what had happened many times when I was a kid.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: But, wow, see how I burst it open? That was cool.
He throws a few punches in the air excitedly.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Ho! Ho! Ha ...! Ah!
He takes back his fist, content, and casually pokes the fire.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: So, in the end, my dad was just telling nonsense to a kid.
The flame is dancing in his eyes.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Those so-called profound teachings, like one needs "adequate strength" or "a sense of responsibility" ...

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Those were too abstract for a kid to understand. Ha, that's indeed his style!

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: But, in the end, the door was opened. That's for sure.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That's a good ending for a story. At least a million times better than mine.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: Haha, you have a long way to go before reaching the end! But I'd say you're in a much better place now than you were in the beginning.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: It's good progress. Trust me.
Observed from the top of the mountain, the old village is only as small as half a palm.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: He who only stays behind a closed door will turn away many things, including a chance to survive.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Alright, alright! Best roast rabbit ever! Ms. Sherjah, you have the first bite!

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: A person with no family yet radiates the warmth of family to others.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: *sighs* … If only Kumar had the slightest warmth from someone, maybe such an absurd thing would have never happened.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: I doubt she's upset about what happened. Maybe she has found herself a good seat to enjoy this dance of Shiva!

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That's true. She is the kind of person who always finds herself the best seat to watch the show.

items.speaker: Shamane
items.text: But, I'm curious. Tell me, did she say anything bad about me?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That was not a part of our conversation. She just admitted that she was being vindictive.
Kaalaa Baunaa slightly frowns, hoping to find some clues in the chaotic memories.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: "Maybe I was being vindictive out of hatred, like you said."
She suddenly jumps up, as if she were burned by the bonfire.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: "Like you said"?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: The Realm can never extract every word I've said. It's theoretically impossible.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: How ... Where-where did she hear that part?
